## Cloudflare: AI bot policies for Search, Agent and Training
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/cloudflare

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Cloudflare: AI bot policies for Search, Agent and Training

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · method

Short answer Cloudflare sorts AI bots into three behaviors: Search, Agent and Training. For each you choose Block on all pages, Block on pages with ads, or Allow, under Security Settings, then Configure AI bot policies. Its page, last updated 1 July 2026, says updated defaults for new domains start on 15 September 2026.

On this page Where the setting is on Cloudflare
Three behaviors, three choices and a date that has already passed
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Shopify
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Cloudflare

In the Cloudflare dashboard go to Security Settings, then Configure AI bot policies. Each of the three behaviors gets its own setting. This works at the network level, so it applies whatever platform the site runs on.

Three behaviors, three choices and a date that has already passed

Cloudflare's presets are: Search, crawlers that collect or index your content to answer questions about it later; Agent, automated activity acting in real time on a person's behalf, such as chat fetch bots and browser-use agents; Training, crawlers taking your content to train or fine-tune a model, including mixed-purpose crawlers used for both Training and Search. Each preset blocks verified bots classified that way plus some unverified bots that behave similarly. The page, last updated 1 July 2026, announces new defaults for new domains from 15 September 2026: Training and Agent bots blocked on pages that display ads, Search remaining allowed, and mixed-purpose crawlers blocked by every configuration that blocks AI training, including the legacy Block AI bots option, which it marks as deprecating on that date. The page still used future tense when we read it on 21 October, five weeks after that date, so open your own dashboard and look at what is switched on rather than trusting either text.

In the vendor's words: “Search: crawlers that collect or index your content to answer questions about it later.”

Source: Cloudflare Docs: Block AI Bots , read on 21 October 2026.

The steps

Open your zone in the Cloudflare dashboard and go to Security Settings.
Open Configure AI bot policies.
For Search, Agent and Training pick Block on all pages, Block on pages with ads, or Allow.
If you use the legacy Block AI bots option, check which mixed-purpose crawlers it now covers, because Cloudflare says it is deprecating.
Test with the free AI-crawler access checker : a bot that robots.txt allows can still be refused here.

The lines to use

To allow:

# Cloudflare settings are not robots.txt lines.
# Choose Allow (do not block) for Search so answer engines can fetch pages.

To block:

# Cloudflare settings are not robots.txt lines.
# Choose Block (on all pages) for Training; leave Search on Allow.

Gotchas

The risk for a shop that wants citations is the middle preset: Cloudflare defines Agent as chat fetch bots acting on a person's behalf, which is the job of fetchers like ChatGPT-User . Blocking Agent can stop an assistant opening your page when a person asks about it, even when your robots.txt allows it. Also note that Shopify says it does not recommend a proxy configuration in front of a Shopify store.

Compare with Shopify

Shopify : Says it handles bot management itself and advises against a proxy.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Does Cloudflare's AI block override robots.txt?

Cloudflare's page describes blocking by behavior at its network, so a bot can be refused there even where your robots.txt allows it. That is why a live request test matters.

What is the difference between Search and Training on Cloudflare?

Search crawlers index content to answer questions later; Training crawlers take content to train or fine-tune a model. Mixed-purpose crawlers are classed as Training.

Is Block AI bots still available?

Cloudflare marks it as deprecating on 15 September 2026. Its page was still written in future tense when we read it on 21 October 2026.

Sources

Cloudflare Docs: Block AI Bots , read 21 October 2026

## Framer: upload your own robots.txt with Static Files

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Framer: upload your own robots.txt with Static Files

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · method

Short answer Framer generates a robots.txt for every published site. To allow or block AI crawlers you upload your own file through Static Files, with the path set to /. Framer says this is available on Pro and Enterprise plans, and that your upload replaces the generated file rather than adding to it.

On this page Where the setting is on Framer
The one thing Framer's page says that the other platforms do not
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Webflow
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Framer

In your project dashboard, select your domain, open the Files tab and upload your file with the path set to /. Framer's help page calls this Static Files. To see the live file first, add /robots.txt to your site's domain in a browser.

The one thing Framer's page says that the other platforms do not

Framer gives you no robots.txt editor. The file is generated for you, and the only way to change it is to upload a replacement, which is limited by plan. Framer's page says that if you need a custom robots.txt you can upload one using Static Files, and that the new file replaces the automatically generated one. The plan limit comes straight after.

In the vendor's words: “This is available on Pro and Enterprise plans.”

Source: Framer Help: Access your robots.txt file , read on 24 October 2026.

The steps

Write your robots.txt as a plain text file on your computer.
Go to your project dashboard and select your domain.
Open the Files tab.
Upload your file with the path set to /.
Open yourdomain.com/robots.txt in a browser to confirm the live file is yours.

The lines to use

To allow:

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

Gotchas

Because your upload replaces the generated file, anything the generated file contained is gone unless you copy it first. Framer's page does not say what the generated file contains, so read yourdomain.com/robots.txt before you upload and keep any lines you want, such as a sitemap line. The page is about robots.txt in general and does not mention AI crawlers by name, so the user agents above are examples to check against each vendor's own page. It was last updated on 15 September 2026.

Compare with Webflow

Webflow : Rules are typed into a settings field rather than uploaded as a file, plus a Content-Signal header.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Can I edit the robots.txt file in Framer?

Yes, by upload. Framer's page says to open the Files tab for your domain in the project dashboard and upload your file with the path set to /. It says this is available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Does Framer create a robots.txt automatically?

Yes. Framer's page says it generates a robots.txt file for every published site, and that a custom file uploaded through Static Files replaces the default one.

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Ghost: add robots.txt to your theme to allow or block AI crawlers

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · 2 sources · method

Short answer Ghost serves a default robots.txt. To change it, save your own robots.txt at the root of your theme, then install and activate the new theme version. Ghost's help page says custom themes on Ghost(Pro) need the Creator plan or higher, so your plan decides whether you can edit it.

The lines to use

Where the setting is on Ghost

There is no robots.txt field in the admin. Ghost's help page says the file lives inside your site's theme: write your robots.txt and save it to the root of the theme. Ghost's theme documentation says the same in one line: themes can include a robots.txt which overrides the default robots.txt provided by Ghost.

The one thing Ghost's page says that the other platforms do not

On Ghost the file travels with the theme, so the plan you are on decides whether you can change it. Ghost's help page says it requires you to be comfortable writing your own robots.txt and installing a new version of your theme. It then adds a plan limit for Ghost(Pro), Ghost's hosted service: installing a custom theme requires the Creator plan or higher. The page describes what happens next in these terms.

In the vendor's words: “Once the new version of the theme is installed and activated, the theme's robots.txt will be used in place of Ghost's default robots.txt.”

Write your robots.txt file.

On Ghost(Pro), check your plan first: Ghost says installing a custom theme requires the Creator plan or higher.

The page also warns that this route needs you to be comfortable writing the file yourself, and it does not cover AI crawlers by name.

At the root of your theme. Ghost's help page says that once the new theme version is installed and activated, the theme's robots.txt is used in place of Ghost's default.

Do I need a paid plan to edit robots.txt on Ghost(Pro)?

Ghost's page says installing a custom theme on Ghost(Pro) requires a subscription to the Creator plan or higher. Because the file is part of the theme, that applies to a custom robots.txt too.

## Netlify: block AI crawlers with robots.txt and User Agent Blocker
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/netlify

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Netlify: block AI crawlers with robots.txt and User Agent Blocker

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · 2 sources · method

Short answer Netlify gives you two routes. One is a robots.txt file served from the root of your site. The other is the User Agent Blocker extension, which uses a Netlify Edge Function to block requests by user agent. Netlify's developer guide says robots.txt alone is not enough, because some AI products ignore it.

On this page Where the setting is on Netlify
The one thing Netlify's pages say that the other platforms do not
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Cloudflare
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Netlify

There is no robots.txt editor in the dashboard pages we read. Netlify's developer guide says to state your rules in a robots.txt file "served from the root of your site". The separate docs page on blocking AI crawlers covers the User Agent Blocker extension, which you find under Extensions in your project's left navigation after installing it.

The one thing Netlify's pages say that the other platforms do not

Netlify's own guide treats robots.txt as the first of two layers, not the whole answer. It shows a robots.txt with one User-agent and Disallow block per bot, generated from a JSON list of names, and then adds an Edge Function that compares each request's User-Agent header with the same list and returns HTTP 401 to a match. It says some AI products do not respect robots.txt, and then adds that the user agent check has a gap of its own.

In the vendor's words: “Sadly, some bots have been found to mis-report their names in their User Agent strings, so we can’t rely on that technique alone either.”

Source: Netlify Developers: Blocking AI bots and controlling crawlers , read on 24 October 2026.

The steps

Write a robots.txt with a User-agent line and Disallow: / for each bot you want to block, and serve it from the root of your site. The guide generates the file from a list of names with a small build script, to avoid typos.
Deploy the site. The guide notes that AI crawlers "should" honor the file, which is why it adds a second layer.
For the extension: in your Netlify project dashboard select Extensions in the left sidebar, search for User Agent Blocker, select it, and select Install. This makes it available for all projects on your Netlify team.
Go to the project where you want it active. You can only activate the extension for one project at a time. Under Extensions in the left navigation, select User Agent Blocker.
Under Block User Agents, select the traffic to block. To target AI crawlers and bots, select all of the AI crawler options.
Select Redeploy site and confirm with Save, then select Enable analytics and deploy site. Netlify says blocking starts working immediately once the deploy succeeds.

The lines to use

To allow:

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

Netlify's pages only show Disallow rules. The Allow lines above are standard robots.txt, not something Netlify documents.

Gotchas

Netlify says the extension's preset list "does not include all possible AI crawlers and AI bots", so a crawler missing from the list is not blocked. The same page lists SEO and search crawlers alongside the AI ones, so select only the AI options if you still want search traffic. The guide's example Edge Function answers with a 401 for every matching request, across the whole site.

Compare with Cloudflare

Cloudflare : A network-level switch that works whatever the site platform is, where Netlify's extension is per project.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Is robots.txt enough to block AI bots on Netlify?

Netlify's guide says no. It says not all AI products respect robots.txt and recommends adding an Edge Function, or the User Agent Blocker extension, that blocks by user agent. It also says some bots mis-report their user agent, so the two layers together are its answer.

Can I turn on the User Agent Blocker for every project at once?

Not according to Netlify's docs. Installing it makes the extension available for all projects on your team, but you can only activate it for one project at a time.

Sources

Netlify Developers: Blocking AI bots and controlling crawlers , read 24 October 2026
Netlify Docs: Block AI crawlers and bots , read 24 October 2026

## PrestaShop: robots.txt generator writes one rule set for all bots
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/prestashop

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

PrestaShop: robots.txt generator writes one rule set for all bots

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · method

Short answer PrestaShop's user guide describes a Robots file generation tool under Shop Parameters, Traffic, SEO and URLs. It writes exclusion directives for non-public files with User-agent: *, so it names no AI crawler. Clicking Generate robots.txt replaces any existing file, so add your own AI crawler rules only after generating.

On this page Where the setting is on PrestaShop
The one thing PrestaShop's page says that the other platforms do not
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Shopify
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on PrestaShop

PrestaShop 8's user guide places it under Configuring your Shop Parameters, then Traffic, then SEO and URLs. The section is called Robots file generation. The page does not name a menu path inside the back office beyond that, and it shows "Last updated 4 years ago" at the foot.

The one thing PrestaShop's page says that the other platforms do not

PrestaShop does not give you a box to type rules into. It gives you a button that writes the whole file. The guide says the generator "simply creates a file with exclusion directives for files and directories that are not meant to be public", applied to all bots through the "User-agent: *" string. It also says the worst bots ignore the file, because it is "purely advisory". The consequence for AI crawlers is in the last two sentences of the section: regenerating wipes whatever you added.

In the vendor's words: “Clicking on the "Generate robots.txt" button replaces any existing robots.txt file with a new one. Therefore, if you want to add your own rules, do it after PrestaShop has generated its version of the file.”

Source: PrestaShop 8 User Guide: SEO and URLs , read on 24 October 2026.

The steps

Open SEO and URLs in the Traffic section of Shop Parameters.
Go to Robots file generation.
Click Generate robots.txt. This replaces any existing robots.txt file.
Add your own rules after PrestaShop has generated its version. The page does not say how to edit the generated file, so use whatever file access your hosting gives you.
Open /robots.txt on your shop to check that your rules are still there. Repeat step 4 every time you click the button again.

The lines to use

To allow:

# Nothing to add: the generated file only lists files and directories that are not public.
# To name one explicitly, add after the generated block:
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

Gotchas

The generated file speaks to every bot the same way, because it uses User-agent: * and nothing else, so PrestaShop's tool gives you no per-crawler choice. The guide says some bots you want to have full access, such as Google's, and others you do not, such as spam bots and content thieves, which is a decision you make in your own added groups. The guide does not mention AI crawlers by name at all, and it points to no setting or module for them.

Compare with Shopify

Shopify : A robots.txt.liquid template that keeps your additions, where PrestaShop's button overwrites them.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Will regenerating robots.txt in PrestaShop delete my AI crawler rules?

Yes, if you added them to the generated file. PrestaShop's guide says the button replaces any existing robots.txt with a new one, and that you should add your own rules after it has generated its version.

Does PrestaShop block AI crawlers by default?

The guide does not say so. It describes a generated file with exclusion directives for non-public files and directories under User-agent: *, and it names no AI crawler.

Sources

PrestaShop 8 User Guide: SEO and URLs , read 24 October 2026

## Shopify: allow or block AI crawlers, and what robots.txt misses
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/shopify

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Shopify: allow or block AI crawlers, and what robots.txt misses

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · 2 sources · method

Short answer On Shopify you control AI crawlers by adding a robots.txt.liquid template to your theme. Shopify's help page says a block there affects only open-web discoverability: product data still goes to agentic storefronts such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot through Shopify Catalog, independently of /robots.txt.

On this page Where the setting is on Shopify
The one thing Shopify's page says that the other platforms do not
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Squarespace
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Shopify

Online Store, then the theme's Edit code, then Add a new template and choose robots. Shopify says this is an unsupported customization: its Support cannot help with edits, and incorrect use "can result in loss of all traffic".

The one thing Shopify's page says that the other platforms do not

Shopify describes two layers of control. The network layer is handled by Shopify for stores on Shopify, and you do not need to act. The /robots.txt layer is yours through robots.txt.liquid. Its page then draws the line that matters for a shop: if you sell through agentic storefronts such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, your product data is syndicated through Shopify Catalog "independently of /robots.txt", and blocking AI crawlers at either layer "affects only open-web discoverability". To change what Catalog shares you use the agentic storefronts settings, not robots.txt.

In the vendor's words: “Blocking AI crawlers at the /robots.txt or network layer affects only open-web discoverability. It doesn't stop your product data from being sent by Shopify Catalog to the agentic storefronts that you've activated.”

Source: Shopify Help Center: Editing robots.txt.liquid , read on 21 October 2026.

The steps

From your Shopify admin go to Online Store.
For the theme you publish, open the menu and choose Edit code.
Click Add a new template, choose robots, then Create template.
Keep the Liquid that outputs the default rule groups and add your own rules below it. Shopify recommends this over replacing the file with plain text, because plain text goes out of date.
Save in the published theme. Shopify says changes are instant, but crawlers do not always react immediately.

The lines to use

To allow:

# Nothing to add: Shopify's default robots.txt allows crawlers that are not named.
# To name one explicitly, add under the default Liquid block:
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

Gotchas

Two details from the same page. A theme uploaded from the Themes section of the admin does not import robots.txt.liquid; ThemeKit or command-line changes keep it. And if your template outputs the default groups, delete it to pick up Shopify's current default, which can include rules your older copy lacks, such as Disallow: /search.

Compare with Squarespace

Squarespace : One checkbox instead of a template, and a fixed list of 26 names.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Does blocking GPTBot on Shopify stop ChatGPT showing my products?

Not by itself. Shopify says robots.txt and network blocks affect open-web discoverability only, and that Shopify Catalog sends product data to the agentic storefronts you have activated independently of /robots.txt. To control that feed, use Shopify's agentic storefronts settings.

Can Shopify Support fix my robots.txt.liquid?

No. Shopify's page says Support cannot help with edits to the file and suggests hiring a Shopify Partner.

Do I need a Cloudflare proxy in front of Shopify?

Shopify says bot management at the network layer is handled for stores on Shopify and that it does not recommend a proxy configuration in front of Shopify or support one.

Sources

Shopify Help Center: Editing robots.txt.liquid , read 21 October 2026
Shopify.dev: Customize robots.txt.liquid , read 21 October 2026

## Squarespace: the AI crawler box blocks 26 bots but not ChatGPT
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/squarespace

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Squarespace: the AI crawler box blocks 26 bots but not ChatGPT

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · method

Short answer Squarespace has one checkbox, Settings, then Crawlers, then Block known artificial intelligence crawlers. It adds 26 named bots to your robots.txt. The list includes GPTBot, ClaudeBot and DuckAssistBot but not OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User or PerplexityBot, and you cannot edit robots.txt yourself.

On this page Where the setting is on Squarespace
The 26 names, and which ones are missing
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Wix
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Squarespace

Open the Settings panel, click Crawlers, and tick Block known artificial intelligence crawlers. Squarespace's page says ticking the box updates your robots.txt file for the bots listed below, and that it may add more over time.

The 26 names, and which ones are missing

Squarespace's help page lists exactly 26 names: AI2Bot, Ai2Bot-Dolma, aiHitBot, Amazonbot, anthropic-ai, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, ClaudeBot, cohere-ai, cohere-training-data-crawler, DuckAssistBot, FacebookBot, Google-Extended, GoogleOther, GoogleOther-Image, GoogleOther-Video, GPTBot, img2dataset, Meta-ExternalAgent, MyCentralAIScraperBot, omgili, omgilibot, Quora-Bot, TikTokSpider and YouBot. Read against our own crawler pages, the box covers the training and dataset crawlers of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Apple, Meta and Common Crawl. It does not name OAI-SearchBot , ChatGPT-User , PerplexityBot , Claude-SearchBot or Claude-User , so ticking it does not remove you from ChatGPT search. It does name DuckAssistBot and Amazonbot , which are answer-engine and product crawlers, so ticking it can also cost you DuckDuckGo's AI answers.

In the vendor's words: “Checking the box updates your robots.txt file to tell the following bots not to crawl your site.”

Source: Squarespace Help: Request that AI models exclude your site , read on 21 October 2026.

The steps

Open the Settings panel of your Squarespace site.
Click Crawlers.
Tick Block known artificial intelligence crawlers to block the 26 names, or leave it unticked to leave them all allowed.
To ask for another bot to be added, contact Squarespace: your page's own text says you can request it.

The lines to use

To allow:

# Squarespace sites are open to these crawlers while the box is unticked.
# You cannot add lines yourself, so there is nothing to paste.

To block:

# Written by Squarespace when the box is ticked (excerpt):
User-agent: GPTBot
User-agent: ClaudeBot
User-agent: CCBot
Disallow: /

Gotchas

Squarespace states that ticking the box does not retroactively remove content already scraped from your site from AI model training data. It also says robots.txt is only a request that friendly crawlers have offered to obey. The excerpt above is our shortened illustration of the kind of lines the box produces; the exact file is whatever your site serves at /robots.txt, so open it and read it.

Compare with Wix

Wix : A real robots.txt editor, and an example list of four names.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Can I allow ChatGPT search but block training on Squarespace?

Partly. Ticking the box writes a rule for GPTBot, and OAI-SearchBot is not among the 26 names. You cannot add lines of your own, so open your live /robots.txt to confirm what it says.

Can I edit robots.txt on Squarespace?

Squarespace's own page treats the Crawlers panel as the control and does not offer a robots.txt editor. Wix and Webflow do.

Does the box stop Google from indexing my site?

No. It is separate from the search engine crawlers option in the same panel. The AI box names Google-Extended and GoogleOther, not Googlebot.

## Vercel: the AI Bots ruleset in the Firewall (Log or Deny)
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/vercel

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Vercel: the AI Bots ruleset in the Firewall (Log or Deny)

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · 2 sources · method

Short answer Vercel handles AI bots with a Firewall ruleset, not a robots.txt line. In your project open Firewall, then Rules, and set the AI Bots Ruleset to Log or Deny. It is available on all plans and starts inactive, shown as Allow, so nothing is blocked until you change it.

On this page Where the setting is on Vercel
The one thing Vercel's page says that the other platforms do not
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Cloudflare
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Vercel

From your project's dashboard, open Firewall in the sidebar, then Rules. In the Bot Management section you will find the AI Bots Ruleset rule. Vercel's docs say the ruleset is available on all plans.

The one thing Vercel's page says that the other platforms do not

Vercel's list of AI bots is not yours to maintain. The ruleset covers AI bots that crawl for training data, search purposes or user-generated fetches, and Vercel keeps the list current. The same page says the ruleset is inactive by default and labelled Allow in the dashboard, so matching traffic is not evaluated and reaches your application. The control is one action for the whole ruleset, Log or Deny, applied at the Firewall.

In the vendor's words: “When new AI bots emerge, Vercel automatically adds them to its managed list and handles them according to your existing configured action without requiring any changes on your part.”

Source: Vercel Docs: Bot Management , read on 24 October 2026.

The steps

From your project's dashboard, open Firewall in the sidebar.
Open Rules in the sidebar.
In the Bot Management section, select Log or Deny on the AI Bots Ruleset rule. Log records AI bot traffic without blocking it and is useful for monitoring. Deny blocks all traffic identified as coming from AI bots.
When you make a change, a Review Changes button appears with the number of changes. Select Review Changes, check them, then select Publish to apply the changes to your production deployment.

The lines to use

Vercel's pages describe this as a Firewall setting, so there is no robots.txt line to add. The two states are:

To allow:

AI Bots Ruleset: Allow (the default, ruleset inactive)

To block:

AI Bots Ruleset: Deny

Gotchas

Deny blocks all traffic identified as coming from AI bots, and the ruleset's scope is training, search and user-generated fetches together, so it is not a way to block training bots while keeping search bots. Log is the safer first step. Vercel's page does not say how the ruleset relates to your robots.txt, so check what your own file says separately. For individual bots, the same page says you can block some or all of the bots in its verified bots directory with WAF custom rules that use the User Agent match condition or the Signature-Agent header.

Compare with Cloudflare

Cloudflare : Also a network-level switch, with three actions for each of Search, Agent and Training.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Does Vercel block AI bots by default?

No. Vercel's docs say the AI Bots Ruleset is inactive by default, labelled Allow in the dashboard, and that matching traffic is not evaluated and reaches your application.

Do I have to keep Vercel's list of AI bots up to date?

No. Vercel says the list of known AI bots is automatically maintained and updated by Vercel, and that new bots are handled according to the action you have already set.

Sources

Vercel Docs: Bot Management , read 24 October 2026
Vercel Docs: WAF Managed Rulesets , read 24 October 2026

## Webflow: robots.txt rules and the Content-Signal header for AI
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/webflow

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Webflow: robots.txt rules and the Content-Signal header for AI

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · 2 sources · method

Short answer Webflow puts robots.txt in Site settings, then SEO, then Indexing, and one of its help pages says you need a Site plan or a paid Workspace plan. It can also send a Content-Signal header that sets ai-train, search and ai-input separately. Webflow calls that a proposed extension, not an accepted standard.

On this page Where the setting is on Webflow
A header that splits training, search and AI answers
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Wix
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on Webflow

Go to Site settings, then SEO, then Indexing, add the robots.txt rule or rules you want, then click Save and publish your site. Webflow adds a sitemap line by default; a toggle removes it.

A header that splits training, search and AI answers

Besides robots.txt, Webflow's page says a site can serve a Content-Signal HTTP header, set in the same Indexing area, to give AI crawlers more granular instructions. Its example is Content-Signal: ai-train=no, search=yes, ai-input=no . Webflow explains the split: robots.txt controls whether bots can access your pages, while Content-Signal says whether content can be used for AI training, search indexing, or AI-generated responses, separately. Webflow adds the caveat itself: this is based on a proposed extension to RFC 9309 and is not yet an accepted standard. So it states a preference; it does not stop a crawler, and Webflow's page does not say which crawlers read it.

In the vendor's words: “This is based on a proposed extension to RFC 9309 and is not yet an accepted standard.”

Source: Webflow Help: Set robots.txt rules , read on 21 October 2026.

The steps

Open Site settings and go to SEO, then Indexing.
Type the robots.txt rules you want in the rules field.
Optionally set the Content-Signal header in the same area.
Click Save and publish your site, then open yourdomain.com/robots.txt to check the live file.

The lines to use

To allow:

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: *
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

Content-Signal: ai-train=no, search=yes, ai-input=no

Gotchas

Webflow's page says your robots.txt is publicly visible, so do not rely on it to hide private pages, and that not all bots follow it.

Compare with Wix

Wix : A longer editing path and a four-name example.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Do I need a paid plan for robots.txt on Webflow?

One Webflow help page says you need a Site plan or a paid Workspace plan to add a robots.txt file to your site.

What is Content-Signal?

A proposed extension to RFC 9309 that Webflow can send as a header: ai-train, search and ai-input, each set to yes or no.

Does Webflow block bad bots for me?

Its help page shows how to write a rule for a named bot. It says some bots, especially malicious ones, do not follow robots.txt.

Sources

Webflow Help: Request to block specific bots from visiting your site , read 21 October 2026

## Wix: block AI crawlers in the Robots.txt Editor (four names)
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/wix

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

Wix: block AI crawlers in the Robots.txt Editor (four names)

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · 3 sources · method

Short answer Wix lets you edit robots.txt: SEO & GEO in the dashboard, then Tools and settings, then Robots.txt Editor. Its help page pastes four names to block: CCBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User and BingAI. ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended are not in that example, so add them yourself if you want them blocked.

On this page Where the setting is on Wix
The example blocks four names, and one of them is not on Bing's list
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Webflow
Check your own site
Questions people ask

Where the setting is on Wix

In your site's dashboard go to SEO & GEO, scroll to Tools and settings, click Robots.txt Editor, then View File. Wix's separate editing guide calls this an advanced feature and says Wix Customer Care cannot help with changes you make to the file.

The example blocks four names, and one of them is not on Bing's list

Wix's help page says its list "includes some known AI crawlers, but you can always add more". The four it prints are CCBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User and BingAI. It leaves out the Anthropic, Perplexity, Google and Meta tokens that appear on our other pages. "BingAI" is the odd one: Microsoft's page on which crawlers Bing uses, read the same day, lists Bingbot, AdIdxBot, BingPreview, MicrosoftPreview and BingVideoPreview and no BingAI. A rule for a name that no crawler uses does nothing, so treat Wix's list as a starting point and check it against each vendor's own page. Also note ChatGPT-User is the fetcher that opens a page for a person asking ChatGPT, so blocking it removes that route to your pages.

In the vendor's words: “This list includes some known AI crawlers, but you can always add more as needed.”

Source: Wix Help Center: Blocking AI Crawlers from Your Site , read on 21 October 2026.

The steps

Go to SEO & GEO in your site's dashboard.
Scroll to Tools and settings and click Robots.txt Editor.
Click View File, then click the field under Your robots.txt file.
Add the directives under This is your current file, then Save Changes and Save.
For one page only, open the page's SEO basics, Advanced SEO, Robots meta tag, and tick nosnippet. Wix says this prevents the content being used as direct input for AI overviews.

The lines to use

To allow:

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: CCBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

Gotchas

Wix's FAQ says blocking AI crawlers in robots.txt may limit NLWeb functionality, because AI agents need access to your structured content. It also says some crawlers ignore robots.txt, so a block is not airtight.

Compare with Webflow

Webflow : Also a robots.txt editor, plus a Content-Signal header.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Will blocking AI crawlers hurt my Wix SEO?

Wix says blocking specific AI crawlers should not significantly affect SEO, and recommends checking your analytics afterwards.

Is BingAI a real crawler?

It is not on Microsoft's current list of Bing crawlers, which names Bingbot, AdIdxBot, BingPreview, MicrosoftPreview and BingVideoPreview. See the Bingbot page .

Does nosnippet block AI crawlers?

Wix describes it as preventing your content being used as a direct input for AI overviews. It is a page-level tag, not a crawler block.

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

WordPress.com: AI opt-out is a privacy setting, not robots.txt

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · 2 sources · method

Short answer On WordPress.com, the AI opt-out is a privacy setting rather than a robots.txt edit. Its site visibility guide, last reviewed on 5 October 2026, says to opt out of sharing your public content with third parties, including AI models, you follow its Prevent third-party sharing guide.

On this page Where the setting is on WordPress.com
Opting out of AI is a sharing setting here
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with Cloudflare

Sources

Where the setting is on WordPress.com

WordPress.com's visibility guide sends you to Settings, then Reading, for Site Visibility (Public, Coming Soon or Private), and to a separate Prevent third-party sharing guide for the AI opt-out.

Opting out of AI is a sharing setting here

WordPress.com's guide on controlling your site's visibility says: to opt out of sharing your site's public content with third parties (including AI models), visit the Prevent third-party sharing guide. That is a platform setting, separate from the robots.txt that search and AI crawlers read. The same page, last reviewed on 5 October 2026, also describes the opposite direction: you can connect external AI agents such as ChatGPT or Claude to read and edit your site's visibility settings by enabling MCP tool access. We could not read the body of the Prevent third-party sharing guide on 21 October: the page loaded with its title and a review date of 1 August 2024 but no steps, by a plain fetch and in a browser. So this page does not describe how that setting works; open the guide from your own dashboard. If you run self-hosted WordPress rather than WordPress.com, the file is yours to edit, as on any host.

In the vendor's words: “To opt out of sharing your site's public content with third parties (including AI models), visit the Prevent third-party sharing guide.”

Source: WordPress.com Support: Control your site's visibility , read on 21 October 2026.

The steps

Open Settings, then Reading, and check Site Visibility is Public if you want crawlers to see the site at all.
Open WordPress.com's Prevent third-party sharing guide from the privacy settings help and follow it if you want to opt out of sharing content with third parties, including AI models.
Open yourdomain.com/robots.txt and read what your site actually serves to crawlers.

The lines to use

To allow:

# No edit to make on WordPress.com for the sharing opt-out.
# Check what your site serves:
# https://yourdomain.com/robots.txt

To block:

# On a self-hosted WordPress site, you add lines like these through your SEO plugin or the file:
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

Gotchas

A Coming Soon or Private site is not the same as an AI opt-out: it hides the site from everyone, search engines included, which is the opposite of what a shop that wants to be cited needs.

Compare with Cloudflare

Cloudflare : A network-level switch that works whatever the site platform is.

Is the WordPress.com AI opt-out the same as blocking GPTBot?

WordPress.com describes it as opting out of sharing your public content with third parties, including AI models. It does not describe it as a robots.txt rule, so check your live robots.txt to see what crawlers are told.

Can I edit robots.txt on WordPress.com?

We did not find a robots.txt editor in the visibility guide we read, so we do not say either way. Look in your site's settings for your plan.

What is MCP tool access?

The guide says it lets external AI agents read and edit your site's visibility settings. It is about managing the site, not about crawlers.

## WP Engine: robots.txt, 10-second default crawl-delay, Web Rules
Source: https://citedby.eu/platforms/wp-engine

AI crawler settings by platform / AI crawlers by platform

WP Engine: robots.txt, 10-second default crawl-delay, Web Rules

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · 2 sources · method

Short answer WP Engine's robots.txt page says a physical robots.txt in your site root overrides any file a plugin or theme generates. Its default file sets a crawl-delay of 10 seconds, and sites on a wpengine.com address get a disallow-all file. To deny a bot by user agent, WP Engine points to its Web Rules Engine.

On this page Where the setting is on WP Engine
The one thing WP Engine's page says that the other platforms do not
The steps
The lines to use
Gotchas
Compare with WordPress.com
Check your own site
Questions people ask
Sources

Where the setting is on WP Engine

WP Engine's page gives two ways to make the file. With the Yoast SEO plugin installed, go to SEO, then Tools, choose the file editor and select Create robots.txt file. Or create a robots.txt file yourself and upload it with SFTP or the SSH Gateway to the root directory of your site. For blocking by user agent, the page sends you to access rules in the Web Rules Engine in the User Portal.

The one thing WP Engine's page says that the other platforms do not

WP Engine ships a default robots.txt, and the page says what is in it. Its note says the default crawl-delay for all sites is 10 seconds, and any environment on a wpengine.com address gets a file that disallows everything, to stop a site being indexed on the wrong domain before launch. Only environments using a custom domain will see changes made to robots.txt. A physical file you upload also takes priority over a file made by a plugin or theme.

In the vendor's words: “This is what’s in the server’s default robots.txt file and can be overridden when you add a custom robots.txt file with one of the methods outlined in this article.”

Source: WP Engine Support: Robots.txt and WordPress , read on 24 October 2026.

The steps

Create a file named robots.txt. The name must be lowercase and the extension .txt, not .html.
Add your directives and save. For a plugin route instead, use Yoast SEO, Tools, then Create robots.txt file.
Upload the file with SFTP or the SSH Gateway to the root directory of your site.
Open /robots.txt on your live custom domain to check it. A copy on a wpengine.com address will not show your changes.
To deny a bot at the server instead, open the Sites page in the User Portal, select the environment, click Web Rules in the secondary left menu (you may have to expand Advanced), choose Access rules and click Add Rule.
Set Action to Deny, IP to All, and add a condition with Type Header, Name User-Agent, Operator Regex matches (~) and the user agent name as Value. Click Add Rule to save.

The lines to use

To allow:

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

To block:

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

WP Engine's page says directive values are case-sensitive and that globbing and regular expressions are not fully supported in robots.txt.

Gotchas

The page names no AI crawlers: its examples use BadBotName, Googlebot, bingbot and SEMrush. It also says robots do not have to follow robots.txt, and recommends a firewall such as Sucuri WAF or Cloudflare, or contacting Support, to stop bad actors before they reach the site. A request denied by a Web Rules access rule gets a 403 Forbidden response and is not counted towards billable visits, per the Web Rules Engine page. Your custom robots.txt overrides the default file, including its 10-second crawl-delay line, so add a Crawl-delay line yourself if you want to keep one.

Compare with WordPress.com

WordPress.com : An AI opt-out in privacy settings rather than a robots.txt file you write.

Check your own site

The free check in the box above reads robots.txt for the AI crawlers and sends one live request per crawler, so a rule that your platform's settings allow but a firewall refuses shows up. The full list of crawlers is on the AI crawler hub .

Questions people ask

Why does my staging site on WP Engine ignore my robots.txt?

WP Engine says sites on an environment.wpengine.com address get a disallow-all robots.txt automatically, and only environments with a custom domain see changes to the file. Shared accounts can add a custom domain only to Production, so Staging and Development usually will not show your edits.

Does a robots.txt plugin override a file I upload to WP Engine?

No, the other way round. WP Engine says a physical robots.txt in the root of your site overwrites any dynamically generated file created by a plugin or theme.

WP Engine Support: Web Rules Engine , read 24 October 2026

## Fail a deploy when AI crawlers can't read your site
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/ai-crawler-check-in-ci

Guides / Crawlability

How to fail a deploy when AI crawlers can't read your site

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-24 · 2 sources · method

Short answer Run the free citedby-check command or GitHub Action after each deploy. It loads your live site from outside, without JavaScript. It exits with 1 when robots.txt blocks one of five crawler names, the home page has very little text, or structured data is missing. It checks the home page and at most one product page.

On this page What can shut AI crawlers out after a deploy?
What does the check look at?
Run it once from a terminal
Add it to GitHub Actions
What a pass does not tell you
What is sent to citedby.eu?
Prefer no dependency?
Questions people ask
Sources

What can shut AI crawlers out after a deploy?

Three changes can do it, and a look at the finished site shows none of them.

A robots.txt written for staging ships to production with a blanket Disallow: / . Under User-agent: * it applies to every crawler that has no group of its own ( RFC 9309 ).
A rewrite moves the page text into JavaScript. A visitor sees the full page, and a crawler that does not run JavaScript receives an almost empty shell. The check below reads the HTML as the server sends it, without running scripts, so it sees what such a crawler sees.
A new CDN or firewall rule refuses the crawler. The check below cannot see this one, and the section on limits says how to test it.

OpenAI says its search systems can take about 24 hours to adjust after a robots.txt update ( OpenAI ). Catching a bad file at deploy time shortens that exposure.

How common is a robots.txt that shuts these crawlers out? In run 1 of our EU AI-Access Index , 15.3% of 10,426 popular EU websites blocked GPTBot. Of the same sites, 7.9% blocked at least one crawler that builds an AI answer index (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot or PerplexityBot). The index records what each file asks AI crawlers to do. We treat blocking a training crawler such as GPTBot as a legitimate choice, and a later section shows how to keep one on purpose.

Source: CitedBy AI-Access Index, run 1. robots.txt of 10,426 of 14,650 sites read on 23 Oct 2026.
What does the check look at?

citedby.eu loads robots.txt , your home page and llms.txt with a plain HTTP request, the way a crawler without a browser does. If the home page links to a product page, or the site has a Shopify product feed, it loads one product page too.

The check runs from outside your pipeline. Source: README and code of citedby-check 0.1.0.
Check What it looks at Result
Crawlers in robots.txt Whether OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended or Bingbot is shut out of the home page. A server error (5xx) on robots.txt counts as shut out, as RFC 9309 says OK, Fix or Not checked
Text in the HTML Words a crawler reads without running JavaScript: 200 or more is OK, 50 to 199 is Check, 1 to 49 is Fix. No readable text at all is Not checked OK, Check, Fix or Not checked
Business data Organization, LocalBusiness or a similar business type as JSON-LD on the home page OK, Fix or Not checked
Product data Product JSON-LD with price, availability and barcode on one product page, when the check finds one OK, Check, Fix or Not checked
llms.txt Whether the site serves a real text file at /llms.txt: more than 50 characters, not an HTML page OK or Optional

Google-Extended is a robots.txt switch only: no crawler fetches pages under that name, so the check reads whether robots.txt allows it.

A missing llms.txt is reported as Optional and never fails a build. We do not expect the file to change what assistants answer ( Does llms.txt work? ).

Run it once from a terminal

You need Node 18 or newer and git. The package is not on the npm registry yet, so the command runs straight from GitHub:

npx github:resaleiq/citedby-check yoursite.com

To keep it installed, run npm install -g github:resaleiq/citedby-check , after which the command is citedby-check . The jq examples below assume it.

Here is a real run on example.com from 23 October 2026. --yes skips the install prompt of npx, --source none keeps the run out of the count of CLI uses, and --no-color keeps the text plain. It exits with 1 because two checks need a fix. Run the same way on citedby.eu, it printed 4 of 4 checks passed. and exited with 0.

$ npx --yes github:resaleiq/citedby-check example.com --source none --no-color
AI-search readiness check for example.com
citedby.eu loaded the site from outside: plain HTTP, no JavaScript.

OK AI crawlers allowed in robots.txt
No robots.txt found, so nothing is blocked.
FIX Text in the page HTML
Only 27 words are readable without JavaScript. Fix: render the
homepage text on the server, so a crawler that does not run
JavaScript still reads it.
FIX Organization data (JSON-LD)
No Organization or LocalBusiness data. Fix: add it as JSON-LD on
the homepage with your name, logo, address or contact and social
profiles, so assistants get your basic facts from one place.
NOT CHECKED Product data (JSON-LD), Price in product data, Availability in
product data, GTIN or barcode in product data
No product page was found from the home page, so product data was
not checked.
OPTIONAL llms.txt
No llms.txt. Optional hygiene: it is cheap to add, but we do not
expect it to change what AI assistants answer.

1 of 3 checks passed. 2 to fix.
This is a technical check. It does not tell you whether an AI assistant will
name your site.

The full audit crawls your site up to your plan's page limit and gives the exact
fix for each problem:
https://citedby.eu/?url=example.com
$ echo $?
1

A line that starts with FIX fails the build: the exit code is 1.
NOT CHECKED is never counted as a pass. No product page was found here, so nothing was scored.
With no robots.txt file (HTTP 404) nothing is blocked, so the crawler check is OK. A robots.txt that answers a server error counts as blocked for all five names, as RFC 9309 says, and a robots.txt that cannot be loaded is NOT CHECKED.

The exit codes are:

0: nothing at or above the level you set.
1: a check needs a fix.
2: wrong use, such as a missing address or an unknown option.
3: not measured: a bad address, the rate limit, a busy citedby.eu, a site that refused or did not answer, or no usable answer.

A check that did not run is never reported as a pass.

--fail-on warn also fails on Check, and --fail-on never exits 0 whenever the check ran, which gives you a report without a gate. --json prints the raw result, so you can list the failing checks in a script:

citedby-check yoursite.com --json | jq -r '.checks[] | select(.status == "fail") | .id'

Add it to GitHub Actions

Create .github/workflows/ai-readiness.yml with the workflow below.
Set url to the public address of the live site, and choose when it runs: weekly, after each deploy, or both.
Open the run page after the first run and read the job summary and the annotations.

name: AI-search readiness
on:
schedule:
- cron: '0 6 * * 1'
workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
check:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
- uses: resaleiq/citedby-check@v0
with:
url: https://example.com

The step fails when a check comes back as Fix. It writes the result to the job summary and marks each problem as an annotation. It also sets the outputs result ( pass , check , fix or not-measured ), passed , total , fix-count and check-count . The README suggests running it after a deploy or on a schedule. For a deploy trigger, see the workflow on our CI page : it uses deployment_status , which runs after Vercel, Netlify or Render reports a deploy.

Annotations on the public run page of the Action's own smoke test against example.com. The errors come from a step with the default setting, the warnings from a step set to report only. A fifth item, a GitHub notice about runner images, is cropped.
Run it against the live address after the deploy. citedby.eu checks from outside, so localhost , private network addresses and pages behind a login cannot be checked. The free check limits how often one site, and one connection, can be checked each hour. A run that hits the limit is reported as not measured with a warning, and it fails your build only when fail-on-error is true .

What a pass does not tell you

It covers the home page and at most one product page.
A pass means a crawler can read the pages the check loads. It does not say that an AI assistant will mention or cite your site.
It reads robots.txt rules and sends one kind of request. A CDN or firewall rule that refuses GPTBot by name is invisible to it. To test that, compare two requests as described in Is GPTBot blocked on my site? . The AI-crawler access checker sends a live request per crawler.
A home page that sends no text at all is reported as Not checked. The check treats an empty answer as a fetch it cannot judge. A run with no failed check still exits with 0. To fail on that case too, test for the status unknown in the JSON:

citedby-check yoursite.com --json --fail-on never | jq -e '[.checks[] | select(.status == "fail" or .status == "unknown")] | length == 0'

If you block GPTBot on purpose, the crawler check reports Fix on every run. OpenAI treats its crawlers separately, so a site can allow OAI-SearchBot and disallow GPTBot ( OpenAI ). The command has no setting to ignore one crawler. With --fail-on never the command itself does not exit with 1, so jq decides. This filter fails only on checks other than a GPTBot-only block:

citedby-check yoursite.com --json --fail-on never | jq -e '[.checks[] | select(.status == "fail") | select(.id != "crawlers" or ((.blocked - ["GPTBot"]) | length > 0))] | length == 0'

What is sent to citedby.eu?

The address, the language code and a tag ( cli , or action in the Action) go to citedby.eu. The request also names the tool and its version in the User-Agent header, and your IP address reaches citedby.eu as with any request. citedby.eu loads your site from its own servers. It adds one to a daily counter for the tag and one to its total count of checks. The command has no telemetry, no cookies and no account, and writes no files. A run tagged none is not counted under cli or action . The check still runs and still counts in the total. The README has the details.

Prefer no dependency?

The shell script on that CI page requests your site with each crawler's own user-agent string. It runs on your machine or in your CI, calls no AI model and sends nothing to CitedBy. It does not read JSON-LD or llms.txt.

Questions people ask

Does the check run my JavaScript?

No. It loads robots.txt, the home page and llms.txt with a plain HTTP request and counts the words a crawler reads without running JavaScript: 200 or more is OK, 50 to 199 is Check, 1 to 49 is Fix.

Does a pass mean AI assistants will cite my site?

No. A pass means a crawler can read the pages the check loads, which are the home page and at most one product page. It does not say that an assistant will mention or cite your site.

Can I block GPTBot and still pass the check?

Not by default. The crawler check reports Fix on every run while GPTBot is blocked, because the command has no setting to ignore one crawler. The section on limits shows a jq filter that fails the build only on other checks.

Does the check need an account?

No. The command has no account, no cookies and no telemetry, and writes no files. The address, the language code and a tag go to citedby.eu, which loads your site from its own servers.

## Can ChatGPT read my website? What decides it
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/can-chatgpt-read-my-website

Guides / Crawlability

Can ChatGPT read my website?

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-18 · method

Short answer ChatGPT can read your website if three things hold: robots.txt does not block OAI-SearchBot, the page text is in the HTML your server sends rather than added by JavaScript, and your server or firewall does not refuse the crawler. The CitedBy audit tests the first two on every page.

On this page The three gates
How to check, step by step
What a blocked page looks like to a crawler
The gate the audit cannot see
What to do with the result
Questions people ask
Sources

The three gates

ChatGPT search uses a crawler called OAI-SearchBot to find pages. OpenAI also runs GPTBot, which collects training data, and ChatGPT-User, which fetches a page when a person asks about it. OpenAI says each is controlled separately in robots.txt, so you can allow one and block another ( OpenAI crawler documentation ).

The audit tests gates 1 and 3. Gate 2 needs your server logs.
How to check, step by step

Open yourshop.com/robots.txt in a browser. Look for User-agent: OAI-SearchBot , GPTBot or * followed by Disallow: / . A blanket Disallow: / under User-agent: * blocks every crawler that has no rule of its own.
Run the free check in the box above. It reads robots.txt for OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Bingbot and tells you which are blocked.
Look at the word count it reports for the page HTML. Your homepage should have hundreds of words there, including your brand name and what you sell.
Open the page, choose "View page source" and search for your product name. If it is missing, the page builds its text with JavaScript and a crawler that does not run scripts sees nothing.
Check that Organization data (JSON-LD) is present, so assistants get your name, logo and contact details from one place.

A real run on bbc.com, 18 Oct 2026. The BBC blocks these crawlers on purpose; for a shop that wants to be named, a result like this is the problem to fix.
What a blocked page looks like to a crawler

Some shop themes and website builders send an almost empty page and fill it in with JavaScript. A visitor sees a full product page. A crawler that does not run JavaScript receives a shell.

Illustration with invented example values.
Some assistants do run JavaScript and some do not, so the safe position is to have your brand and product text in the HTML itself.

The gate the audit cannot see

robots.txt is a request, and your hosting is the enforcement. A firewall or CDN setting can answer a crawler with an error even when robots.txt allows it. The audit does not test this. Look in your server or CDN logs for requests from OAI-SearchBot and see which status codes came back; a run of 403 responses is the sign.

What to do with the result

robots.txt blocks a crawler you want: remove the matching Disallow rule. OpenAI says changes can take about a day to take effect.
Few words in the HTML: render the homepage and product text on the server.
No Organization data: add it as JSON-LD on the homepage.
All clear: being readable is the entry ticket, not the result. Whether an assistant names your shop is a separate question, which the audit measures by asking real buyer questions.

Questions people ask

Is GPTBot the same as ChatGPT search?

No. GPTBot collects data that may be used to train models. OAI-SearchBot is the crawler for ChatGPT search results. You can block GPTBot and still allow OAI-SearchBot.

If I block GPTBot, will ChatGPT stop mentioning my shop?

Not by itself. Search results depend on OAI-SearchBot. Blocking only GPTBot is a common choice for shops that do not want their content used for training.

Does adding llms.txt fix this?

It is optional. We do not expect it to change what assistants answer, and the audit marks it as optional.

How long until a change shows up?

OpenAI says it can take about 24 hours for its systems to adjust after you change robots.txt.

## ChatGPT shows my old price: find the source and fix it
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/chatgpt-wrong-price

Guides / Wrong facts

ChatGPT shows my old price. How to find where it read it and fix it

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-18 · 4 sources · method

Short answer ChatGPT shows an old price when it read that price from a stale source: your own page, a product feed, or another website. Search for the old price in each place, fix the source, then ask again twice in a new chat. Update your feed whenever a sale starts or ends.

On this page Why an assistant quotes a price you changed
Step 1: write down the wrong answer
Step 2: look for the old price on your own page
Step 3: check your product feed
Step 4: search for the old price on other websites
Step 5: wait, then re-ask
Can the audit find this?
Questions people ask
Sources

Why an assistant quotes a price you changed

An assistant answers from what it can find: pages it fetched, feeds a merchant submitted, and third-party pages that mention you. If one of those still carries the old figure, the answer can carry it too. That makes a wrong price a data problem on a page you control or can contact, which is why it can be fixed. The fix happens at the source, not in the chat.

A reader on r/ecommerce described exactly this on 22 September: ChatGPT recommended a bundle that had been discontinued a year earlier, at the old $149 price ( thread ). It is one report, not a measured rate, so treat it as an illustration of the pattern.

Check the three sources in this order: your page, your feed, then other sites.
Step 1: write down the wrong answer

Open a new chat, with web search on if the assistant offers it, and ask: "What does [product] from [shop] cost?" Copy the answer, the date, the assistant and any link it cites. A cited link is the best clue, because it names the page that fed the answer. Ask a second time in another new chat. If the two answers differ, log both, since answers vary between runs.

Step 2: look for the old price on your own page

Open the product page and view the page source (right click, View page source).
Search for the old price, for example 49.00 . Try with and without the currency sign.
Find the application/ld+json block and read the offers price. Product markup that was never updated is a common reason for a stale figure, and Google says the price in markup and feed must match the landing page ( Google Merchant Center help ).
Look for a second price on the page: a "was" price, a bundle price, a variant that loads a different amount.
Fetch the page the way a crawler does, with no JavaScript. If the price only appears after scripts run, a crawler may not see the final figure. Google's help page also warns that slow pages can make crawlers miss the final price.

Step 3: check your product feed

If you sell through Google Shopping, a marketplace or ChatGPT's shopping feed, the feed is a second copy of your price. OpenAI's product feed specification asks for a price in the form 79.99 USD , one row per purchasable item or variant, and says to update the feed when a sale starts or ends ( OpenAI product feed spec ). A sale that ended on your site but stayed in the feed is the classic mismatch.

Google describes the same trap for its own feed: when the feed and the landing page disagree, the fix is to match them, resubmit through feed upload, the Content API or your shop platform, and then request a review, which Google says takes 7 business days ( Google Merchant Center help ). OpenAI's page does not describe a way to dispute data already ingested, so we do not promise one.

Step 4: search for the old price on other websites

Search the old price together with your brand name and product name. Look at review sites, price lists, comparison pages, old blog posts and your own press releases. Ask the owner of each page to update it. Where you cannot, publish a current page on your own site that states the price with the date, so the newest source is also the clearest one.

Step 5: wait, then re-ask

OpenAI says a robots.txt change can take about 24 hours to reach its search crawler ( OpenAI crawler documentation ). It publishes no schedule for refreshing a page it has already read, so nobody can promise you a date. Re-ask the same prompt twice, in new chats, once a week, and log each answer in a table.

Fix the source, not the chat. Then log every re-test.
Date Assistant Prompt Price shown Link cited Matches your page?
2026-10-18 ChatGPT, search on What does [product] from [shop] cost?

Can the audit find this?

The CitedBy audit crawls your pages and tests whether AI crawlers can reach them and read your product data. If your price page is blocked or empty to a crawler, no fix to the price can help, so test that first.

Questions people ask

Why does ChatGPT show an old price for my product?

It probably read the old figure from your page, your product feed or another website that still carries it. Search the old price in each place and look at the link it cites, if there is one.

How long until ChatGPT shows the new price?

Nobody can promise a date. OpenAI says robots.txt changes take about 24 hours to reach its search crawler, and it gives no refresh schedule for pages already read. Re-ask weekly and log the answers.

Can I ask OpenAI to change a wrong price?

OpenAI's feed specification does not describe a way to correct data already ingested, so fix the sources instead and re-test. Check OpenAI's help centre for any report option that exists when you read this.

Does a price in schema markup matter?

Yes, when it is stale. Google says markup and feed price should match the landing page, and a markup block that was never updated is a common mismatch to look for.

## What does ChatGPT say about your brand? 20 prompts
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/check-what-ai-says-about-your-brand

Guides / Brand checks

What does ChatGPT say about your brand? 20 prompts to check it by hand

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-18 · method

Short answer To check what ChatGPT says about your brand, ask it 20 prompts in four groups: your brand, your category, comparisons with rivals, and facts such as price and shipping. Ask each twice in a new chat, log whether it names you, links you and gets the facts right, and count the results.

On this page What to prepare
The 20 prompts
How to score each answer
What to do with your log
The faster way
Questions people ask
Sources

What to prepare

You need a free account on each assistant you care about, a spreadsheet, and about an hour. Open a new chat for every prompt so earlier answers do not colour the next one, and turn web search on if the assistant offers it, because an answer built from live pages can differ from one without. Write down which assistant, which setting and the date. Answers change between runs, which is why every prompt gets asked twice.

Fill the brackets with your own words: [category] is what you sell (for example "natural latex mattresses"), [country] is where you ship, [brand] is your shop name and [rival] is a shop you compete with.

The 20 prompts

Group A: your brand (does it know you?)

Prompt Ask this
P1 What is [brand]?
P2 Is [brand] a good place to buy [category]?
P3 What do customers say about [brand]?
P4 Where is [brand] based and where does it ship?
P5 What does [brand] sell and what is it best known for?

Group B: your category (are you named?)

Prompt Ask this
P6 Where can I buy [category] online in [country]?
P7 Which online shop is best for [category] in [country]?
P8 Which shop delivers [category] fast in [country]?
P9 What should I buy as a gift: [category], and from where in [country]?
P10 Which small or independent shops sell good [category] in [country]?

Group C: comparisons (who beats you?)

Prompt Ask this
P11 [brand] or [rival] for [category]?
P12 What are alternatives to [rival] for [category] in [country]?
P13 Is [brand] cheaper than [rival]?
P14 Which shops are similar to [brand]?
P15 Why would I choose [brand] over a big marketplace for [category]?

Group D: facts (is it right?)

Prompt Ask this
P16 How much does [brand] charge for [your best-selling product]?
P17 Does [brand] still sell [a product you discontinued]?
P18 What is [brand]'s return policy?
P19 How much is shipping from [brand] to [country]?
P20 Does [brand] have a physical shop?

Copy this layout into a spreadsheet. The rows shown are invented examples.
How to score each answer

Run the prompt and save the full answer text and every link.
Mark named when your brand name or your domain appears in the answer text or in its links. If you appear as a link only, still mark it, and note it.
Mark linked when a link goes to your own domain.
Copy every other shop that is named. Rivals that appear again and again are your real competition in that assistant.
For groups A and D, check every fact against your own site and mark the ones that are wrong or old.
Run the same prompt once more in a new chat and log it as run 2.

Do not round up. A shop named in 1 of 2 runs is named in 1 of 2 runs, not "recommended".

What to do with your log

Named in few group B answers: the assistant does not connect your shop to your category. Look at which pages it links for those answers; they are the pages it trusts.
Wrong facts in group D: fix the source it read. Prices and policies on your own pages come first, then third-party listings.
Rivals named again and again: open the pages the assistant linked for them and note what they contain that yours lacks.
Nothing named anywhere, including your brand: check first that assistants can read your site at all ( Can ChatGPT read my website? ).

The faster way

Twenty prompts across five assistants is 200 manual runs. A CitedBy audit works on your site instead: it crawls up to your plan's page limit, shows which pages assistants cannot read or quote, and gives the exact fix for each. The audit starts at €9.

Questions people ask

Do I need ChatGPT Plus to run these prompts?

No. A free account is enough to see what a free user sees. Paid plans can answer differently, so note which plan you used.

Why ask every prompt twice?

Answers vary between runs. Two runs show whether a result is stable; one run can be luck.

Should I ask for my brand by name in every prompt?

No. Groups B and C test whether you are named when the buyer does not know you yet, which is the case that brings new customers. Groups A and D test what is said once they do.

How often should I repeat this?

After each change to your site and about once a month. Log the date every time so you can compare.

## Cloudflare blocking AI crawlers? How to allow them (2026)
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/cloudflare-ai-crawlers

Guides / Crawlability

Cloudflare is blocking AI crawlers on my site. How to allow GPTBot and ClaudeBot

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-19 · 4 sources · method

Short answer In the Cloudflare dashboard, open your domain, then AI Crawl Control, then the Security tab. Find each crawler, such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot, and choose Allow in the Actions column. Blocking creates a WAF rule, so removing it means switching the crawler back to Allow. Then run a check from outside.

On this page Why Cloudflare can block AI crawlers without you touching robots.txt
Allow a crawler in Cloudflare, step by step
Which crawler to allow for which goal
How to confirm it worked
Should you allow everything?
Questions people ask
Sources

Why Cloudflare can block AI crawlers without you touching robots.txt

Cloudflare sits in front of your shop and can refuse a crawler before your server sees the request. That is why a robots.txt that welcomes every bot does not settle the question. When you choose Block for a crawler in AI Crawl Control, Cloudflare creates or updates a WAF custom rule on your zone to enforce it ( Cloudflare docs ).

Defaults are moving too. Help Net Security reports that from 15 September 2026 the default settings for new domains block Training and Agent crawlers on pages that display ads, while Search crawlers stay allowed. Cloudflare said it would notify customers before the change. That date has passed, so read your own dashboard instead of guessing which default your domain has ( Help Net Security ).

Allow a crawler in Cloudflare, step by step

Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain.
Open AI Crawl Control, then the Security tab.
Find the crawler in the table, for example GPTBot or ClaudeBot.
In the Actions column choose Allow. The same menu offers Block.
If you also want robots.txt rules honoured, enable Enforce robots.txt. Cloudflare says this stays available when you allow a crawler.
Run the free check below on your homepage, then repeat the two-request test from our GPTBot guide .

The setting sits under AI Crawl Control, not under the general firewall rules.
Two details from Cloudflare's documentation. A blocked crawler can be answered with a 403 or a 402 code and a custom message, and changing that response is available on paid plans only. Free plans can still allow and block.

Which crawler to allow for which goal

OpenAI and Anthropic each publish three crawlers with different jobs. Allowing the search crawler is the usual way to be findable, and you can treat the training crawler as a separate decision.

Job OpenAI Anthropic
Collect content that may train models GPTBot ClaudeBot
Improve search results OAI-SearchBot Claude-SearchBot
Fetch a page because a person asked ChatGPT-User Claude-User

Same three jobs at both companies. Allow or block them one by one.
Anthropic says its bots follow robots.txt and support Crawl-delay. It publishes the IP ranges its crawlers use at claude.com/crawling/bots.json , and warns that blocking by IP address alone may stop the bot from reading your robots.txt ( Anthropic help centre ). OpenAI publishes its crawler list and IP ranges in its documentation ( OpenAI ).

How to confirm it worked

Cloudflare changes are not proof until a request gets through. Three checks, in order:

Run the free check in the box above. It reads robots.txt for the main AI crawlers and tells you if your page answers a plain request.
Send two requests with curl, one normal and one with a crawler user-agent, and compare the status codes. The commands are in our GPTBot guide .
Look at your server or Cloudflare logs a day later for the crawler's name and the status codes it received.

If the dashboard says Allow but the second request still returns 403, look for a second rule: a security plugin, a hosting firewall or an older WAF rule can refuse the same traffic.

Should you allow everything?

Not necessarily. Blocking training crawlers while allowing search crawlers is a legitimate setup, and Cloudflare's own defaults lean that way for pages with ads. What costs shops is blocking by accident. A site that blocks the search crawlers cannot be fetched for those search features, so decide per crawler and write down why.

Questions people ask

Where is the AI crawler setting in Cloudflare?

Open your domain, then AI Crawl Control, then the Security tab. Each crawler has an Actions column with Allow and Block.

How do I unblock ClaudeBot in Cloudflare?

Find ClaudeBot in the crawler table on the Security tab and choose Allow. Anthropic also lists Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User as separate crawlers, so check those rows too.

Does allowing a crawler in Cloudflare override my robots.txt?

No. Cloudflare says you can still enforce robots.txt after allowing a crawler. A Disallow rule in your robots.txt still tells that crawler to stay away.

Is the 15 September 2026 default change affecting my shop?

Help Net Security describes it as a change to the defaults for new domains. If your domain is older, your existing settings stand until you change them. Check the Security tab to see what applies.
