## Does llms.txt work? What the data says (2026)
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/does-llms-txt-work

Guides / AI visibility basics

Does llms.txt work? What two studies and Google's own documentation say

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-23 · 5 sources · method

Short answer So far the evidence says llms.txt does not move AI citations. Ahrefs found 97% of valid llms.txt files got zero requests in May 2026, SE Ranking found no clear link to citations across about 300,000 domains, and Google says you do not need AI text files. Adding one is cheap, but do not expect traffic from it.

On this page What llms.txt is
What the data says
What Google says
So should you add one?
What to do instead first
Questions people ask
Sources

What llms.txt is

llms.txt is a proposal by Jeremy Howard, published in September 2024: a Markdown file at /llms.txt with a title, a short summary and lists of links, meant to give AI agents a concise map of a site ( llmstxt.org ). It is not an official standard of any search engine or AI lab. The proposal's own page lists adoption by documentation platforms and says OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini publish the file for their own developer docs. That shows people write it. It does not show that assistants read yours when they answer a shopper.

What the data says

Figures as reported by Ahrefs. Most requests came from audit tools and unknown bots, not assistants.
Does anything fetch it? Ahrefs checked 137,210 domains with its web analytics in May 2026. It found that 97% of valid llms.txt files received zero requests that month. Of the requests that did arrive, 19.5% came from named AI tools. SEO audit tools, unknown bots and general crawlers made up much of the rest. Ahrefs also reports that no AI bot went looking for the file on sites that did not have one ( Ahrefs study ).

Does it change citations? SE Ranking analysed about 300,000 domains and published in November 2025 that having llms.txt showed no clear connection to how often a domain is cited by AI, with 10.13% of domains having the file ( Search Engine Journal on the SE Ranking study ). Their own wording is that it "doesn't seem to directly impact AI citation frequency. At least not yet."

How common is it on launched sites? In our launch crawl of 300 Show HN sites and 70 Lovable builds (20 and 21 October 2026, CitedBot, no JavaScript), 34% of Show HN sites (100/293) and 18% of Lovable sites (12/66) served an llms.txt file. In the same crawl, 16% of Show HN homepages and 74% of Lovable ones sent under 100 words of text in their HTML. We did not measure citations, so the crawl shows how often the file exists, not what it does.

Both studies are correlation or log data from outside parties, run on different samples with different methods. They support "no measurable benefit so far", not "it can never matter".

What Google says

Google's documentation on AI features states that there are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, and that you do not need to create new machine-readable files, AI text files or markup to appear in them ( Google Search Central: AI features ). For ChatGPT, OpenAI documents the crawlers it uses (OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User) and says robots.txt controls them; it does not describe llms.txt there ( OpenAI crawler documentation ).

So should you add one?

Your site Add llms.txt? Why
Online shop, no developer docs Optional, after the basics The data shows no citation benefit, so fix crawler access and on-page facts first
Software with public docs or an API Reasonable Coding agents and audit tools do fetch it, and Ahrefs saw agents among the requesters
You already have one Leave it, keep it accurate A stale file that lists dead pages helps nobody

If you add one, keep it short: your name, one sentence on what you sell and where you ship, and links to your main category, shipping and returns pages. It takes minutes.

What to do instead first

Run the free check in the box above. It tests whether AI crawlers can fetch your page and read it, and it reports whether an llms.txt exists as a hygiene item, without treating it as a ranking factor.
Put price, shipping and returns in the page text, not only in images or scripts.
Ask an assistant 20 buyer questions twice each and log who gets named ( the method ).

Questions people ask

Does ChatGPT read llms.txt?

There is no published evidence that it does. OpenAI documents its crawlers and robots.txt but does not describe llms.txt, and Ahrefs found most requests to llms.txt files came from other kinds of bots.

Does llms.txt help me get cited by AI?

Not on current evidence. SE Ranking found no clear link across about 300,000 domains, and Google says no AI text file is needed for its AI features.

Can llms.txt hurt?

It can mislead if it is stale or lists pages you removed. Keep it short and accurate, or do not publish one.

Is llms.txt the same as robots.txt?

No. robots.txt tells crawlers what they may fetch. llms.txt is a proposed summary file for AI agents that no major search engine requires.

## GA4: track traffic from ChatGPT and AI assistants
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/ga4-ai-referral-traffic

Guides / Measurement

Is AI traffic converting? How to set up GA4 to see visits from ChatGPT and other assistants

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-19 · method

Short answer Create a custom channel group in GA4 with an AI assistants channel whose Source matches a regex of the assistants you see in your Traffic acquisition report. Move it above Referral, because GA4 uses the first matching channel. Then compare conversions by channel. Visits without a referrer stay under Direct.

On this page What GA4 shows by default, and why AI visits hide
Build an AI assistants channel in GA4
A starter regex, and how to check it
What GA4 cannot tell you
Make the next step visible
Questions people ask
Sources

What GA4 shows by default, and why AI visits hide

GA4 sorts every session into a channel. Visits from an assistant can end up in the Referral channel, mixed with links from blogs and directories, or under another channel, so you cannot see them as a group. A custom channel gives them their own row. Google's documentation describes how: a custom channel group can be applied to your reports retroactively, so history is relabelled as soon as you save it ( Google Analytics Help ).

You need the Editor role or above on the property to create one. Standard properties can hold 2 custom channel groups, with up to 50 channels each, according to the same page.

Build an AI assistants channel in GA4

In GA4, open Reports, then Acquisition, then Traffic acquisition. Change the dimension to Session source / medium.
Scan the list for assistant names such as chatgpt, perplexity, claude, gemini or copilot. Write down the exact sources you see.
Open Admin, then Data display, then Channel groups, and choose Create new channel group.
Choose Add new channel, name it AI assistants, and add a condition group: Source, matches regex, then paste your list of sources.
Save the channel, choose Reorder, and drag AI assistants above Referral. Click Apply.
Reopen Traffic acquisition with your new channel group as the dimension and compare sessions, engaged sessions and conversions.

Order matters: GA4 gives each session to the first channel it matches.
The order step is the one people miss. Google says traffic is included in the first channel whose definition it matches, given the current order. If Referral sits above your new channel, assistants never reach it.

A starter regex, and how to check it

Download the file with the steps and the regex . It starts from the names of the well-known assistants:

(chatgpt|openai|perplexity|claude|gemini|copilot)

Treat it as a starting guess, not a verified list. Hostnames change and assistants launch, so what matters is what appears in your own report. Add the sources you really see, and remove any that match something that is not an assistant. Run the check at least once a quarter.

Match what your own report shows, not a copied list.
What GA4 cannot tell you

Only visits that carry a referrer can be labelled. A person who copies your address from an answer and pastes it into a browser arrives as Direct. A channel in GA4 therefore shows a lower bound of AI-driven visits, not the total. Say so when you report the number to anyone who will act on it.

Small numbers can be noise. Compare conversion rate and revenue per session against Organic Search before drawing any conclusion, and do not extrapolate from a week of data.

Make the next step visible

The channel tells you whether assistants send visitors. It does not tell you whether they name your shop. The free check shows whether AI crawlers can read your pages, and the audit asks real buyer questions to see who gets named.

Questions people ask

How do I see ChatGPT traffic in GA4?

Open Traffic acquisition with Session source / medium and look for chatgpt in the source column. For a standing view, create an AI assistants channel as above.

Why does my AI traffic show as Direct?

When the visitor's browser sends no referrer, GA4 has nothing to label. Pasting a link or opening it from an app without referrer information gives that result.

Does a custom channel group change my old data?

Google says custom channel groups can be applied to your reports retroactively, so yes, your history is relabelled in reports that use the group.

Do I need to be an admin to create it?

No, but you need at least the Editor role on the property.

## GEO vs AEO vs SEO audit: what differs, what you need
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/geo-vs-aeo-vs-seo

Guides / AI visibility basics

GEO audit vs AEO audit vs SEO audit: what is different and which one you need

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-18 · 2 sources · method

Short answer An SEO audit checks whether you rank in search results. An AEO audit checks whether your pages give direct answers that assistants can quote. A GEO audit checks whether AI assistants name your brand in generated answers. The terms have no official definition, and the first two checks feed the third.

On this page The short version
What an SEO audit checks
What an AEO audit checks
What a GEO audit checks
What Google says
Which one a small shop needs first
A five-step order of work
Questions people ask
Sources

The short version

None of the three terms is a standard. Each vendor draws the lines a little differently, so ask what a quoted audit actually tests before you compare prices. The grid below is how we use the words at CitedBy, and the sections after it explain each one.

Our reading of the three terms. Other vendors group the checks differently.
What an SEO audit checks

An SEO audit asks whether search engines can crawl and index your pages and whether those pages deserve to rank for the searches your buyers make. Typical items are crawl access, page speed, titles, internal links, structured data and backlinks. The output is a list of fixes and a set of ranking positions.

What an AEO audit checks

AEO, answer engine optimization, asks whether a page answers a question so directly that a system can lift the answer. Typical items are a short answer under a question heading, FAQ blocks, tables and clear facts such as price, shipping time and returns. It overlaps with SEO, since a page that answers clearly also reads well to a search engine.

What a GEO audit checks

GEO, generative engine optimization, asks whether an assistant such as ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity names your brand when someone asks for a recommendation, and whether what it says is true. The check is run by asking real buyer questions, several times, and counting who gets named, who gets linked and which facts are wrong. A page-level checklist cannot answer that, because the result depends on what the assistant finds across the web.

What Google says

Google's documentation on AI features in Search states that there are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode and no other special optimizations necessary. It adds that the best practices for SEO remain relevant, that a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet, and that you do not need new machine-readable files, AI text files or markup ( Google Search Central: AI features ). That applies to Google's own features. ChatGPT uses its own crawlers, and OpenAI lists three with different jobs: OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT's search features, GPTBot for model training, and ChatGPT-User for actions a person starts ( OpenAI crawler documentation ).

So the honest answer to "is it just SEO?" is: the base is shared, and the part that is new is measuring whether assistants name you.

Which one a small shop needs first

Your situation Start with Why
Pages are not indexed, or the site is slow or empty without JavaScript SEO basics Nothing else works if crawlers cannot read the page
You rank, but pages bury price, shipping and returns AEO fixes Direct facts are what an assistant can quote
You rank and answer well, but buyers ask an assistant and rivals get named GEO audit This is the question only asking the assistant can answer
You are not sure An audit, then 20 prompts by hand The audit shows crawler access on every page, the prompts show what is said

A five-step order of work

Run the free check in the box above and fix any crawler that is blocked or any page that is empty to a crawler.
Make sure price, shipping, returns and a short description sit in the HTML text, not only in images or scripts.
Add a short answer and a FAQ to your top three pages, written in your buyers' own words.
Ask an assistant 20 buyer questions twice each and log who gets named ( the 20-prompt method ).
Fix the sources behind any wrong fact, then repeat the prompts a few weeks later.

Questions people ask

Is GEO just SEO with a new name?

Partly. The technical base is shared, and Google says SEO best practices remain relevant for its AI features. What GEO adds is measuring whether assistants name your brand, which a ranking report does not show.

What is the difference between AEO and GEO?

AEO is about making a page easy to quote as an answer. GEO is about whether an assistant mentions your brand in what it generates. The first is a property of your pages, the second is an outcome you measure by asking.

Do I need an llms.txt file for any of them?

Google says you do not need new machine-readable files or AI text files to appear in its AI features. We cover the evidence for other assistants in a separate guide on llms.txt.

Which audit should I buy first?

Fix crawl access and basic facts first, since you can check those yourself. Buy a GEO audit when you want to know who gets named when buyers ask, and ask the seller what prompts it runs and how often.

## How to create an llms.txt file: 6 steps and a template (2026)
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/how-to-create-an-llms-txt-file

Guides / AI visibility basics

How to create an llms.txt file, step by step

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-21 · method

Short answer To create an llms.txt file, write a plain-text Markdown file with a # title, a short > summary and ## sections that list your key pages as [name](url): note links, save it as llms.txt and upload it to your site root so it loads at yourshop.com/llms.txt. Then run the free checker to confirm it loads and its links work.

On this page What llms.txt is
The format, in order
Template to copy
How to create the file
Mistakes the checker finds
Check the crawlers too
Questions people ask
Sources

What llms.txt is

llms.txt is a proposal published at llmstxt.org : a Markdown file at the root of your site that gives language-model assistants a short map of the pages that matter most. It is not a standard that any search engine or assistant has committed to read. Does llms.txt work? covers what the studies found. The file is cheap to write, and writing it makes you decide which of your pages answer buyers' questions.

The format, in order

The llmstxt.org specification lists these parts in this order. Only the first is required.

A # title with the name of the site or project.
A > blockquote with a short summary.
Optional paragraphs or lists with more detail, but no headings.
Zero or more ## sections, each holding a list of links.
By convention, a section named Optional for links an assistant can skip when it needs shorter context.

Each list item is a Markdown link, then optionally a colon and a note: - [Link title](https://link_url): what this page answers .

Template to copy

Replace the example text with your own. Keep the shape.

# Example Shop
> Example Shop sells handmade leather bags and ships across the EU.

## Products
- [Leather bags](https://example.com/bags): all models with prices and sizes
- [Care guide](https://example.com/care): how to clean and store a bag

## Policies
- [Shipping and returns](https://example.com/shipping): delivery times and the 30-day return rule

## Optional
- [About us](https://example.com/about)

How to create the file

Open a plain-text editor and type the title line: # Your shop name . Keep it to the name buyers know you by.
Add one > line under it that says what you sell and where, in one sentence. Use facts a page of yours also states.
List your most useful pages under ## headings such as Products, Help or Policies. Use full URLs, one link per line, and add a short note after a colon saying what the page answers. Short on time? The free llms.txt generator writes a first draft from your own pages' titles and descriptions for you to edit.
Put pages that are nice to have, such as About or press, under a section named Optional .
Save the file as llms.txt (plain text, UTF-8) and upload it to the root of your site so that https://yourshop.com/llms.txt loads. A file in a subfolder does not count, and the address must answer with text, not a login or an HTML error page.
Run the free llms.txt checker on your domain. It reports whether the file loads, follows the format, links to pages that load, and agrees with your robots.txt and sitemap.

Mistakes the checker finds

The title is missing or is not the first line.
A list item is not in [name](url) form, for example a bare URL.
A listed page returns an error, or robots.txt keeps AI crawlers away from it. A page you list but block sends mixed signals.
A listed page is not in your sitemap.
The address returns an HTML page instead of a text file.

Check the crawlers too

A perfect llms.txt does nothing for a site whose firewall refuses AI crawlers. Run the AI-crawler access checker next: it tests robots.txt and a live request for eight crawlers.

Questions people ask

Where does llms.txt go?

At the root of the domain: https://yourshop.com/llms.txt . Not in a subfolder.

Do I have to list every page?

No. List the pages that best answer buyers' questions. A short, accurate file is better than a long list of everything.

Do ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity read llms.txt?

No major assistant has confirmed that it does. Treat the file as a cheap addition, not as a way to get cited.

What is llms-full.txt?

An optional second file some sites publish with the full text of key pages in one document. The checker only reports whether it exists.

How do I know the file is valid?

Run the free llms.txt checker on your domain.

Sources

## Is GPTBot blocked on your site? 4 ways to check (2026)
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/is-gptbot-blocked

Guides / Crawlability

Is GPTBot blocked on my site? Four places to check, with a test for each

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-18 · 4 sources · method

Short answer GPTBot is blocked on your site if robots.txt has a Disallow rule that applies to it, or if a CDN, firewall or server rule refuses its requests. Open yourshop.com/robots.txt, run an audit, then compare two requests to your server. Blocking GPTBot does not by itself block ChatGPT search.

On this page Four places GPTBot can be stopped
How to check, step by step
The two-request test
Cloudflare: where the setting lives
When the check says your site refused the request
Should you unblock GPTBot?
Questions people ask
Sources

Four places GPTBot can be stopped

GPTBot is the crawler OpenAI says it uses to collect content that may be used to train its models. A request from it can be turned away at four layers, and each one needs its own test. The free check in the box above covers the first. The other three answer with an error code even when robots.txt says yes.

Layers 2 to 4 are invisible in robots.txt, so check them separately.
How to check, step by step

Open yourshop.com/robots.txt in a browser. Look for a group that names GPTBot . If there is none, GPTBot follows the User-agent: * group, so a blanket Disallow: / under it blocks GPTBot too ( RFC 9309 ).
Run the free check in the box above. It reads robots.txt for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Bingbot and names the ones that are blocked.
Send two requests to your homepage and compare the status codes: one normal, one that carries the GPTBot user-agent string. Commands below.
Open your CDN account and look at its AI crawler settings. For Cloudflare, the steps are below.
Open your security plugin or firewall rule list and search for GPTBot , bot , AI and crawler .
Search your server logs for GPTBot . A run of 403 responses to it is the sign of a block that robots.txt does not show.

The two-request test

Replace yourshop.com with your address. The first command sends a normal request, the second sends the GPTBot user-agent string that OpenAI publishes. Each prints only the status code.

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://yourshop.com/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -A "Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot" https://yourshop.com/

A 403 on the second request alone means a rule targets the crawler's name.

Read the result with one limit in mind. This test comes from your own computer. If your host also judges crawlers by IP address, the real GPTBot can get a different answer from the one you saw. OpenAI publishes the IP ranges for GPTBot at openai.com/gptbot.json , so your logs can show whether requests from those ranges got through ( OpenAI crawler documentation ).

Cloudflare: where the setting lives

Cloudflare's documentation describes the steps: open your domain, go to AI Crawl Control, open the Security tab, then the Crawlers tab. The Actions column lets you Allow or Block each crawler. Choosing Block creates or updates a WAF custom rule, and you can still enforce robots.txt when you choose Allow ( Cloudflare: manage AI crawlers ).

Cloudflare's defaults are also changing. Help Net Security reports that from 15 September 2026 new domains block Training and Agent crawlers by default on pages that show ads, while Search crawlers stay allowed ( Help Net Security ). Check your own dashboard rather than assuming which default your domain got.

When the check says your site refused the request

A plain request from our check can itself be refused. When the answer is HTTP 403, 429 or 503, the check says so and says it cannot tell from outside whether AI crawlers are refused as well. A 403 usually means a rule blocked the request. A 429 or 503 can also mean rate limiting or an outage, which affects every visitor. Fix the cause in your CDN, firewall or hosting panel, then run the check again.

Should you unblock GPTBot?

That is your decision, and blocking it is a legitimate choice. OpenAI lists GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User as separate crawlers with separate jobs. GPTBot is for training data. OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT's search features. ChatGPT-User fetches pages when a person asks about them.

Your goal What to do
Appear in ChatGPT search results, keep content out of training Allow OAI-SearchBot , disallow GPTBot
Appear in ChatGPT search results and allow training Allow both
Stay out of both Disallow both and check your logs for ChatGPT-User

A change to robots.txt can take about 24 hours to reach OAI-SearchBot, according to OpenAI.

Questions people ask

Does blocking GPTBot remove my shop from ChatGPT?

Not by itself. OpenAI describes OAI-SearchBot as the crawler for ChatGPT's search features and GPTBot as the training crawler, each set separately in robots.txt.

Why does robots.txt look fine but GPTBot still gets a 403?

robots.txt is a request to the crawler. A CDN, firewall or server rule can refuse the request anyway, so check those layers with the two-request test and your logs.

Does ChatGPT-User obey robots.txt?

OpenAI says robots.txt rules may not apply to ChatGPT-User, because a person starts those requests.

Will unblocking GPTBot get my shop recommended?

No. Being readable is the entry ticket. Whether an assistant names your shop depends on what it finds about your category, which the CitedBy audit measures with real buyer questions.

## Is my website cited by ChatGPT? How to check it
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/is-my-website-cited-by-chatgpt

Guides / Brand checks

Is my website cited by ChatGPT? How to check it, step by step

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-23 · method

Short answer To find out if ChatGPT cites your website, run four checks: its crawlers can fetch your pages, Bing holds them in its index, ChatGPT names or links you when you ask the questions your buyers ask, and chatgpt.com shows up as a referrer in your analytics. A failure at step one or two explains most silence.

On this page The four checks
What stops sites at step 1
What stops sites at step 2
What to do with the result
The faster way
Questions people ask
Sources

The four checks

Reach. Open your robots.txt and look for rules on GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User, then fetch your homepage without JavaScript and count the words. The AI crawler checker does both for free.
Index. ChatGPT search draws on search-engine results from partners, and Bing is the one most often named, so check that Bing and Google hold your pages: add your site to Bing Webmaster Tools and Google Search Console, submit the sitemap, and run URL Inspection on your homepage.
Answers. Ask ChatGPT, logged out and in a new chat, the questions your buyers ask ("where can I buy [what you sell] in [country]?"). Write down whether it names you, links you and gets your facts right. Use the 20-prompt list .
Visits. In GA4 or your server logs, filter referrers for chatgpt.com. A cited page sends clicks; a mention without a link may not.

What stops sites at step 1

We fetched 300 sites that launched on Show HN (15 to 20 October 2026) and 70 built with Lovable, as CitedBot, with robots.txt obeyed and no JavaScript. The launch crawl found:

Check Show HN Lovable
Homepage under 100 words of text in the raw HTML 16% (47/293) 74% (49/66)
robots.txt blocks at least one of five AI crawlers 4% (12/294) 0% (0/67)
Homepage turned away a live request from one of those crawlers 11% (33/293) 0% (0/66)

So robots.txt was the smaller factor. An empty HTML shell and a firewall that refuses AI user agents turned up more often. These numbers say nothing about whether those sites are cited; we did not measure that.

What stops sites at step 2

A page that no index holds cannot be found by a search-backed answer. On 22 October 2026 Bing's own URL Inspection reported the home pages of three of our sites as "Discovered but not crawled". Discovered means Bing knows the URL and has not fetched it yet. Submitting the sitemap and the IndexNow protocol on every publish shortens the wait; it does not set a date.

What to do with the result

Step 1 fails: fix robots.txt rules or the firewall first, then make the homepage send its text in the HTML.
Step 2 fails: submit the sitemap, request indexing and ping IndexNow, then check again in a week.
Step 3 shows rivals, not you: open the pages ChatGPT linked for them and note what they hold that yours lacks.
Step 4 shows nothing: one week is too short to judge; log the date and repeat monthly.

The faster way

The audit crawls your site up to your plan's page limit, shows what AI crawlers cannot read or quote, and gives the exact fix for each issue. It starts at €9. Prefer to check only access first? Run the free check .

Questions people ask

Can I see every time ChatGPT cites my site?

No. OpenAI does not publish a citation report for site owners. Your server logs show its crawlers' requests and visits from chatgpt.com, and asking the questions by hand shows the rest.

Does blocking GPTBot stop ChatGPT citing me?

Not by itself. GPTBot is the training crawler; OAI-SearchBot is the one used for search, and ChatGPT-User fetches pages when a person asks. Check each rule on its own.

How long until a new page is cited?

We cannot give a number. It must first be crawled and indexed, and answers change from run to run.

## Lovable, Bolt or React site empty to AI? Check and fix
Source: https://citedby.eu/blog/vibecoded-site-empty-to-ai

Guides / Crawlability

My Lovable, Bolt or React site looks empty to AI. How to check it and fix it

By the CitedBy editorial team · Reviewed on 2026-10-18 · 3 sources · method

Short answer AI crawlers read the HTML your server sends and, according to Vercel's analysis, do not run JavaScript. A site built in the browser can look empty to them even when it looks perfect to you. Test it by viewing the page source, then switch to server rendering or prerendering if your text is missing.

On this page Why a site that looks fine can be empty to AI
The 30-second test
What Lovable says
Fixes by setup
Two other things to check at the same time
Questions people ask
Sources

Why a site that looks fine can be empty to AI

A site made with an AI app builder is often a single-page app. The server sends a near-empty HTML shell, and JavaScript builds the headline, price and buttons in your browser. A visitor never notices. A crawler that does not run the script receives the shell and nothing else.

Vercel analysed AI crawler traffic across its network and reported that none of the major AI crawlers it looked at render JavaScript. It names OpenAI (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, GPTBot), Anthropic (ClaudeBot), Perplexity (PerplexityBot), Meta and ByteDance. It also reports that ChatGPT's and Claude's crawlers fetch JavaScript files (11.5% and 23.84% of their requests) without executing them, while Gemini uses Googlebot's infrastructure and can render JavaScript ( Vercel: the rise of the AI crawler ). That is one company's measurement from its own network, and crawler behaviour can change, so test your own site instead of assuming.

What a crawler without JavaScript receives, in both setups.
The 30-second test

Open your homepage in a browser, right click and choose View page source (not Inspect, which shows the page after scripts ran).
Search the source for your main headline and one price or product name.
If you find them in the text, crawlers can read them. If you find only a <div id="root"></div> and script tags, the page is empty to a crawler that skips JavaScript.
Run the free check in the box above. It fetches your page with a plain request, without running scripts, and counts the readable words in the HTML.

For a command-line version, curl -s https://yourshop.com/ | head -c 3000 prints the start of what a crawler gets.

What Lovable says

Lovable's FAQ says new apps created from 13 May 2026 (22 June 2026 for Enterprise workspaces) use TanStack Start, which renders pages on the server, and that older apps use React with Vite and render in the browser. For those older apps it says Lovable serves pre-rendered copies of published pages to verified search engines, social preview bots and AI crawlers ( Lovable FAQ ). So a Lovable site may be readable even if it is client-rendered, but that depends on how and where it is published. A custom setup or a copy exported to another host does not inherit it. Check the source on your live address, not on the builder's preview.

We found no equivalent statement from Bolt or other builders, so we make no claim about them. Run the test on each site.

Fixes by setup

Your setup Fix Check afterwards
New Lovable app (TanStack Start) Nothing to switch, rendering is on the server View source on the live address
Older Lovable app (React + Vite) Confirm the live address returns the text, and read Lovable's rendering notes for options View source, and the audit
React + Vite you host yourself Move critical pages to server rendering or prerender them at build time View source on each key page
Next.js Pages and layouts are Server Components by default, which render on the server ( Next.js docs ). Keep price and description out of client-only components View source
Other builder Ask the vendor how published pages are rendered, then test View source

Whatever you choose, the pages that matter are the ones a buyer would ask about: home, category, product, shipping and returns. Put price, availability and a short description in the server-sent HTML and keep scripts for interaction only.

Two other things to check at the same time

Product data: the price and name should also appear as Product JSON-LD in the server HTML, not injected later.
Blocks: a site can be readable and still be refused. See Is GPTBot blocked on my site? .

Questions people ask

Does ChatGPT run JavaScript on my site?

Vercel's analysis found that none of the major AI crawlers, including OpenAI's, render JavaScript. Test your own page with View page source, since behaviour can change.

How do I know if my site is client-side rendered?

View the page source. If your headline and price are not in it, and you see an empty root div with script tags, the page is built in the browser.

Is a Lovable site always empty to AI?

No. Lovable says new apps render on the server and that older apps get pre-rendered copies served to verified crawlers. Check the live address to be sure.

Does Google see my client-rendered site?

Vercel reports Gemini uses Googlebot's infrastructure and can render JavaScript. Other assistants may still read nothing, so server rendering helps with all of them.

Vercel: the rise of the AI crawler
Lovable FAQ: rendering and SEO
Next.js: Server and Client Components
